title: Principal Fitting ideal gives a free open after removing power torsion
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $P$ a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $r\geq0$, $a,h,c\in A$ with $a=hc$, and $\mathfrak q\subset A$ a prime ideal [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume multiplication by $a$ on $A$ is injective. Use localization as in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and Fitting ideals as in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. Suppose
$$ \operatorname{Fit}_r(P_{\mathfrak q})=cA_{\mathfrak q}, $$
and, if $r>0$, suppose $\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(P_a)=0$. Put $Q=P/\Gamma_{(a)}(P)$, where $\Gamma_{(a)}(P)=\{x\in P\mid a^n x=0\text{ for some }n\geq0\}$ [def-nagata-power-torsion]. Then there exists $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $Q_g\cong A_g^{\oplus r}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module].

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, last two proof paragraphs: principal Fitting generators, spreading generators and vanishing of relations; abstracted to an arbitrary ring and prime.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], the images of a finite generating family of $P$ generate $P_{\mathfrak q}$ and its quotient $Q_{\mathfrak q}$. The ring $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is local by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Apply [lem-trf-affine-principal-fitting-generators] to $P_{\mathfrak q}$, $k=r$ and $f=c/1$, using the assumed equality $\operatorname{Fit}_r(P_{\mathfrak q})=(c/1)$. Thus $P_{\mathfrak q}/\ker(c/1)$ is generated by at most $r$ elements.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, penultimate paragraph: apply More on Algebra Tag 080Z to the principal Fitting ideal

proof.text: The fraction map $P_{\mathfrak q}\to Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is surjective, by lifting a numerator. If $x=m/s$ belongs to $\ker(c/1)$, [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $t\notin\mathfrak q$ with $tcm=0$. Since $a=hc$, also $atm=0$, so $tm\in\Gamma_{(a)}(P)$ by [def-nagata-power-torsion]. Hence $x$ maps to zero in $Q_{\mathfrak q}$. The map therefore factors surjectively through the quotient of step 1. Its generators have images $q_i/s_i$ with $q_i\in Q$ and $s_i\notin\mathfrak q$; replacing them by $q_i/1=s_i(q_i/s_i)$ preserves their span. Pad with zero elements to obtain $q_1,\ldots,q_r\in Q$ generating $Q_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, penultimate paragraph: passage from the c-annihilator quotient to the a-power-torsion quotient

proof.text:
Let $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ be the images in $Q$ of finite generators of $P$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For each $j$, write $y_j/1=\sum_i(\alpha_{ij}/s_{ij})(q_i/1)$ in $Q_{\mathfrak q}$. Put $s_j=\prod_i s_{ij}$, so $s_j
otin\mathfrak q$ and all $s_j\alpha_{ij}/s_{ij}$ come from $A$. The fraction zero criterion in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] supplies $t_j
otin\mathfrak q$ such that $t_js_jy_j$ belongs to $\sum_iAq_i$. Put $g=\prod_jt_js_j
otin\mathfrak q$. Every $t_js_j$ is invertible in $A_g$, so the $q_i/1$ generate $Q_g$. Write $B=A_g$ and let $\pi:B^{\oplus r}	woheadrightarrow Q_g$ send the standard vectors to these generators. If $r=0$, surjectivity gives $Q_g=0=B^{\oplus0}$ and finishes the proof. Empty products above mean $1$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, penultimate paragraph, last sentence: explicit spreading of finitely many generators

proof.text: Assume $r>0$. There is a canonical isomorphism $Q_a\cong P_a$: send $\bar m/a^k$ to $m/a^k$. This is well defined because every element of $\Gamma_{(a)}(P)$ is zero in $P_a$ [def-nagata-power-torsion, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. More explicitly, changing a representative or a fraction equality changes its numerator by an element killed by some power of $a$. The map is surjective; if $m/a^k=0$ in $P_a$, some $a^Nm=0$, whence $\bar m=0$ in $Q$, proving injectivity. Inverting also $g$ gives $(Q_g)_a\cong(P_a)_g$, both represented by fractions with denominators $a^kg^l$. Thus localizing $\pi$ gives a surjection $\pi_a:B_a^{\oplus r}\twoheadrightarrow(P_a)_g$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, last paragraph: identify the quotient with the original module after inverting a

proof.text: By base change in [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] applied to $A_a\to(A_a)_g=B_a$, the hypothesis gives $\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}((P_a)_g)=0$. For any $v=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\in\ker\pi$, its image $v/1$ is a relation of the surjection $\pi_a$. The minors description and independence of the surjection in that same cited node identify this Fitting ideal with the ideal of all $1\times1$ minors of rows in $\ker\pi_a$, since $r-(r-1)=1$. Each $b_i/1$ is one such minor, hence is zero in $B_a$. The localization zero criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] yields an integer $N_i\geq0$ with $a^{N_i}b_i=0$ in $B$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, last paragraph: coefficients of relations lie in the lower Fitting ideal; More on Algebra lemma-fitting-ideal-finite-locally-free, converse proof (Tag 07ZD)

proof.text: Multiplication by $a$ remains injective on $B=A_g$: if $a(x/g^k)=0$, [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $g^lax=0$ in $A$ for some $l\geq0$; injectivity on $A$ gives $g^lx=0$, hence $x/g^k=0$. Repeated cancellation, including $N_i=0$, applied to step 5 shows every $b_i=0$. Thus $\ker\pi=0$ and $\pi$ is bijective. Its inverse is linear because uniqueness of preimages preserves addition and scalar multiplication. Consequently $Q_g\cong B^{\oplus r}=A_g^{\oplus r}$, as required [def-weil-pbc-free-module].
